newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Deadline postponed for Bosnian arbitration.
newsitem.headline: Deadline postponed for Bosnian arbitration.

text.p: A deadline for deciding who will control a strategic Bosnian town has been postponed after the Serb side pulled out of the arbitration, international officials said on Monday.

Representatives from Bosnia's Serb republic and Moslem-Croat federation were supposed to agree on the status of the northern town of Brcko by December 14 under terms of the Dayton peace agreement signed a year ago.
But after the Serb member of the three-man arbitration panel pulled out of the talks this month, the deadline was postponed for another 60 days, said a statement issued by the panel.
Brcko is considered Bosnia's most volatile flashpoint and the Dayton peace treaty failed to resolve the dispute over its future status.
The town, seized by Serb forces at the beginning of the 1992- 1995 Bosnian war, lies on a narrow strip of land which links Serb-held territory to the east and west.
The U.S. lawyer chairing the panel and the Moslem-Croat federation representative issued a statement saying the Serb demand for an extension to February 15 had been granted.
The Serb representative, Vitomor Popovic, who pulled out of the arbitration earlier this month, did not sign the statement.
Negotiations over Brcko have failed to make any significant progress and diplomats say the Serb side has tended to avoid meetings.
A spokesman for the office of the High Representative to Bosnia said the Serb withdrawal appeared to cast doubt on their commitment to the arbitration.

"Legally, it makes no sense for one party to simply walk away from the procedure because the whole point of arbitration is that people sign on beforehand to abide by whatever decision is handed down. " spokesman Colum Murphy told reporters.
